newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian dlr sidelined, awaits FOMC meeting.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian dlr sidelined, awaits FOMC meeting.

text.p: The Australian dollar's vigil ahead of the the U.S. FOMC meeting on Tuesday saw it held to a narrow band on Monday around its New York closing levels.
With little on the local calendar in a week shortened by the Good Friday holiday, all eyes in Australian markets, as in the rest of global markets, are on the FOMC.

The meeting is widely expected to lead to an increase in the U.S. Fed Funds rate, a move which analysts said could lead to some short term weakness in the Australian dollar due to narrowing interest rate differentials.

"This suggests scope for some weakness short term, particularly as we think there will be at least a 12 month delay before the RBA follows the Fed," Westpac senior economist Helen Camp said, a view shared by others.

"What will happen is if the Fed does move this week, they'll (the market) probably then factor in another move, possibly two, and that should weaken the Australian dollar in the short term," Bankers Trust senior economist David Bassanese said.
In the middle of last year, before the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) began cutting rates, official Australian short term rates were 225 points over U.S. rates.

The subsequent rate easings, as well as market expectations that countries such as the U.S. and Britain were in tightening cycles, has seen the flow of funds entering Australia chasing high yields slow. This was a factor behind the dollar's fall to a low of US$0.7550 in February.
But while the unit would stumble on a U.S. rate increase, analysts said the reasons behind such a move by the Fed should be supportive of the Australian dollar further out.
"Our longer term view is that the dollar is going to be fairly resilient, the world growth outlook is looking good and also commodity prices look good over 1997/98," Bassanese said.

Westpac's Camp was also bullish on the outlook for the dollar, forecasting a rise above last December's six year high of US$0.8212 by the end of this year, after the initial softness expected to follow the U.S. rate hike had passed.

"By mid-year, however, the very forces behind the Fed tightening -- stronger U.S. growth -- underpin the recovering world growth-rising commodity price story which is the key to our forecast Australian dollar appreciation to US$0.84 by year end," she said.
